articles.title: Where to watch Lakers vs Warriors and what time does Los Angeles' second preseason game start?
articles.standfirst: Warriors and Lakers open the preseason in the Bay: Curry, Dončić and a night of first impressions
articles.summary: Warriors and Lakers open the preseason in the Bay: Curry, Dončić and a night of first impressions
articles.body:
The NBA calendar still doesn’t count for much, but when the Golden State Warriors and Los Angeles Lakers meet, not even a preseason game goes unnoticed. Two of the most closely followed franchises on the planet restart their engines in the San Francisco Bay Area for one of the most attractive matchups at the start of the 2026 NBA Preseason, with familiar faces, new faces, and plenty of curiosity to see how the pieces fit together before the real action begins.

LA Lakers vs Golden State Warriors: Time and where to watch it

The NBA preseason game is scheduled for the night of Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time (9:00 p.m. Central Time and 7:00 p.m. Pacific Time); the Warriors are the home team.

Coverage of this NBA preseason game can be followed on NBC Sports and NBA TV, with local broadcast on SportsNet.

Overview of the NBA preseason game

Preseason is, by definition, a laboratory: long rotations, minutes spread around, and a coaching staff more interested in the processes than in the scoreboard. Even so, the intrigue is there. Golden State arrives with the veteran core that has defined its identity, and the Lakers show up with a rebuilt roster centered around their great European star.

For the Warriors, the focus is on integrating a large, young group. Their registered roster mixes veteran experience with a wave of emerging talent: seasoned names like Draymond Green, Gary Payton II, and Georges Niang coexist with the young crop led by Brandin Podziemski, Moses Moody, Will Richard, and Brazilian Gui Santos.

In the paint, Graham Ike, Charles Bassey, and Dominican Yaxel Lendeborg will battle for minutes, while Alex Toohey, the 22-year-old Australian, is one of the profiles to watch among the younger players on the roster.

On the Los Angeles side, the figure is unavoidable: Luka Dončić, the 27-year-old Slovenian, is the centerpiece around which the entire project revolves. Around him, the Lakers have assembled a group with plenty of depth: Austin Reaves as the starting shooting guard, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes providing points from the perimeter, and an interior rotation strengthened by Walker Kessler, Kevon Looney, and the versatile Jarred Vanderbilt.

The last name that always draws attention, Bronny James (21 years old), is once again looking for his place, and pieces like Jake LaRavia, Dalton Knecht, and Ziaire Williams round out a deep roster of up to 26 registered players.

What does the betting market look like and what is the forecast for Lakers vs Warriors?

The sportsbooks leave little room for doubt about who enters the matchup between the two franchises as the favorite: the Los Angeles Lakers appear as clear favorites with an implied probability of 62.2% (odds of 1.57), compared to Golden State's 37.8% (odds of 2.85).

In the total points market (over/under), the main line stands at 235.5—over at 1.92, under at 2.01—with an alternative line at 237. In the point spread, the Lakers are listed as favorites by between -4.5 and -5.5 points, which confirms the market’s reading.

That said, the preseason forces you to take any prediction with a grain of salt: star players' minutes are usually limited, and the outcome depends as much on the starters as on the young players trying to earn a roster spot.

With that nuance, Los Angeles' favoritism makes sense based on talent and depth, but it would come as no surprise if a game with long rotations were decided by details and ended up more evenly matched than the odds indicate.

The most sensible bet for a night like this is usually the total points: both teams’ up-tempo style and defenses still finding their footing make the over 235.5 worth a close look.

Prediction: narrow victory for the Los Angeles Lakers, with a tighter finish than the favoritism suggests.

articles.title: Former NBA champion reveals three changes Bronny James has made that've turned him into a player to watch
articles.standfirst: Bronny impressed with his defense against Sacramento
articles.summary: Bronny impressed with his defense against Sacramento
articles.body:
There are only so many touches available on a team built around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, which makes the path to playing time for Bronny James fairly clear.

If the Los Angeles Lakers are going to trust him with regular minutes, he has to affect games in other ways.

Against the Sacramento Kings, that meant defending every possession as if it mattered.

James picked up ball-handlers high, stayed attached through actions and repeatedly tried to disrupt passing lanes. One possession, in which he knocked the ball loose and immediately dove to the floor to recover it, prompted a strong reaction from former NBA champion Danny Green on the broadcast.

“Great defense,” Green said. “I think he’s learned a thing or two from being around Collin Sexton in that locker room. "Setting hands on the ball, diving on the floor again, first one to the ground – this is how you earn your minutes. Trying to pick up some weight in the offseason too, he’s got a little stronger.”

That sequence captured why the performance mattered, as James wasn't waiting for the offense to come to him.

Redick has made the assignment clear

The defensive emphasis isn't new.

Head coach JJ Redick has been pushing James to become a more disruptive full-court defender, particularly when the Lakers are trying to create energy without changing the structure of their offense.

“I think just building on defensive instinct, how I was in the playoffs, picking up full court,” James said after a recent practice. “They’ve been emphasizing that, so I’ve been one of the guys that is picking up full court every possession, every time we get a bucket, just picking up full court.”

That responsibility has also carried into practice, where James has regularly drawn difficult assignments against Doncic and Reaves.

“For sure, it’s going to make me better on the defensive end just picking them up full court,” James said. “I’m annoyed by them, they get annoyed with me in practice. Just continuing to do that will make me better for sure.”

James appeared in 42 games last season, but his role remained limited and inconsistent.

The Lakers now have greater backcourt depth, with Collin Sexton expected to take significant minutes behind Doncic and Reaves when healthy. That leaves James in a position where every preseason opportunity carries added weight.

He's unlikely to win those minutes by outscoring the established guards ahead of him.

He can, however, make himself valuable by pressuring the ball, defending the point of attack and bringing the kind of effort coaches notice immediately.

That is what Green was responding to against Sacramento.

“This is how you earn your minutes,” he said.

It was only a preseason performance, but it offered a useful glimpse of what James ’ path could look like.

If he can make defense his calling card, the Lakers may not need him to do much more to justify keeping him on the floor.

articles.standfirst: LeBron James' travel time from New York to Philadelphia is 45 minutes. It would take two hours by car.
articles.summary: LeBron James' travel time from New York to Philadelphia is 45 minutes. It would take two hours by car.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season is right around the corner, with the official tip-off arriving in just two weeks via an opening-day triple-header featuring six projected playoff teams.

The action kicks off as the Eastern Conference 's top-seeded Detroit Pistons host the Boston Celtics , followed by the reigning champion New York Knicks raising their championship banner and receiving their rings ahead of a marquee clash against the revamped Philadelphia 76ers , headlined by marquee offseason additions LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , before the night concludes with a Western Conference Finals rematch between the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder .

Among this star-studded slate, the most captivating matchup undeniably centers on the Sixers and James, who commutes to practice via a 45-minute helicopter ride (see video above) from his primary residence in New Jersey.

Helicopter Commute Puts LeBron James’ Daily Travel Routine in the Spotlight

As an established family man, husband, and father, LeBron has opted for a pragmatic travel solution rather than enduring a grueling two-hour highway drive or relocating his household to Pennsylvania.

The viral simulation video highlights the flight path, showing the aircraft lifting off from the Sixers' practice facility in Camden, N.J. , situated just across the Delaware River from Philadelphia, before ascending over the water and tracking the gray ribbon of the New Jersey Turnpike past local refineries and marshes toward the towering skyline of New York City .

While head coach Nick Nurse plans to carefully regulate his minutes alongside co-stars Joel Embiid , Tyrese Maxey , and Jaylen Brown , James emphasized during Media Day that anything short of pushing past the conference semifinals will be classified as a failure for this ambitious franchise.

articles.title: LeBron James' latest decision is backfiring on him: "He hates Philadelphia so much that he can't spend more than 30 seconds in the city"
articles.standfirst: LeBron James may have found the ultimate way to avoid Philadelphia traffic
articles.summary: LeBron James may have found the ultimate way to avoid Philadelphia traffic
articles.body:
LeBron James’ decision to make New York his home while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers has quickly become one of the NBA’s most talked-about storylines.

After the four-time champion was photographed returning to Manhattan by helicopter following a Sixers scrimmage, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy couldn’t resist taking a shot at him.

“This man hates Philly so much he can’t spend more than 30 seconds in the city,” Portnoy joked on X while reacting to images of James ’ unusual commute.

The reality, however, appears to be more practical than personal. James has reportedly been traveling between New York and Philadelphia by helicopter, turning a road journey that can take anywhere from 90 minutes to two hours into a trip of roughly 30 minutes.

Flight records reviewed by Front Office Sports reportedly showed the aircraft making 12 round trips between the two cities in a single week.

What adds to the story is the fact that James isn’t spending millions of his own money on transportation. His existing partnership with Fanatics includes access to the company’s corporate aviation program.

According to a representative for James , the agreement was established well before he joined the Sixers and allows him to split his time between New York and Philadelphia.

At retail rates, a one-way helicopter trip between the cities can reportedly cost somewhere between $4,000 and $10,000. If James were to use the service for every Philadelphia home game, the theoretical cost could become enormous.

However, the flights reportedly fall under his existing Fanatics agreement.

The commute may actually be about protecting James’ body

There’s another reason the unusual routine could make sense. James is preparing for his record-extending 24th NBA season while dealing with physical issues that require special attention.

ESPN has reported that the veteran is managing chronic arthritis in his left foot while continuing to deal with sciatica in his lower back.

Those concerns are particularly relevant given James ’ age and workload. He’ll turn 42 later this year, and his back problems already caused him to miss significant time last season with the Los Angeles Lakers.

He eventually returned to play 60 games, averaging 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists.

The Sixers should also be able to reduce his workload. James will share the floor with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown , giving Philadelphia several established scoring options and potentially allowing the veteran to conserve energy throughout the season.

James ’ commitment to his new team isn’t in question as V.J. Edgecombe has noted that the veteran regularly arrives at the practice facility before his teammates, sometimes as early as 7:45 a.m.

James has also praised Philadelphia’s famously passionate supporters, describing their relationship as one based on mutual respect.

So, despite Portnoy’s joke, the helicopter commute doesn’t necessarily prove James dislikes the city, though the optics are undeniably amusing.

articles.title: Michael Jordan's Ferrari breaks a record: 2.7 million for the car that inspired his sneakers
articles.standfirst: The 1997 550 Maranello that accompanied Jordan in his final years with the Bulls was out of public view for nearly 24 years and has just become the most expensive of its model ever sold at auction
articles.summary: The 1997 550 Maranello that accompanied Jordan in his final years with the Bulls was out of public view for nearly 24 years and has just become the most expensive of its model ever sold at auction
articles.body:
The Michael Jordan Ferrari already has a new owner and also a new record. The 1997 550 Maranello that belonged to the six-time NBA champion sold for $2.7 million at the JOOPITER auction, which closed on September 30. The price made this example the most expensive of its model ever sold publicly.

The figure far exceeded the initial estimate, which was set between $700,000 and $1.3 million. But the car’s value lies not only in its rarity: it was owned by Jordan, appeared repeatedly in photographs during his final years with the Bulls and, above all, was the inspiration for one of the most famous sneakers of his career.

The Ferrari that ended up transformed into a pair of Air Jordans

When Tinker Hatfield began designing the Air Jordan XIV, he used Jordan's 550 Maranello as a reference. Ferrari's influence was reflected in several elements of the sneaker: the quilted leather recalls the sports car's interior, the car's air intakes are reinterpreted on the sides, and the heel area features a design inspired by the tires.

The most obvious detail is in the emblem. The Jumpman appears inside a shield inspired by Ferrari’s famous prancing horse. The car and the sneaker were thus forever linked by one of Jordan’s last great images with Chicago.

Jordan debuted the Air Jordan XIV during Game 6 of the 1998 Finals against the Utah Jazz. Wearing them, he made the game-winning shot over Bryon Russell with 5.2 seconds left, the famous ‘Last Shot’ that gave the Bulls their sixth championship and became his final shot as a Chicago player.

From the fifth ring to Jordan's garage

Ferrari’s story began a year earlier. The car was delivered to Jordan on May 29, 1997, with Rosso Barchetta bodywork, a beige leather interior, chromed Speedline wheels, and the personalized license plate “MJ 5”. On June 13, just a few hours after winning his fifth NBA championship, Jordan left the United Center behind the wheel of the Maranello, with the trophy and a cigar in his hands.

“The Ferrari was actually used. Jordan put approximately 6,400 miles on it and drove it to Bulls games, practices, and public appearances. His size also made it necessary to carry out modifications to the driver’s seat: the rails were extended and thinner padding was used to allow for a more reclined position.”

Under the hood is a naturally aspirated 5.5-liter V12 with 485 horsepower, paired with a six-speed manual gearbox. But, in this case, the technical specifications are almost overshadowed by the history this particular car has accumulated.

Jordan sold the Ferrari on December 4, 2002 through Lake Forest Sportscars, in Illinois. Then a long disappearance began: for nearly a quarter of a century there were no confirmed public sightings of the car.

The search was led for years by John Temerian, co-founder of CURATED. The definitive lead appeared when a partial chassis number surfaced on an old internet forum. With that information, they were able to reconstruct the full VIN and, through Ferrari’s historical records, locate the car in the hands of a collector in California.

The Ferrari returned to Chicago on May 29, 2026 , exactly 29 years after its original delivery. Among the documentation it retains is the factory warranty card, still bearing Jordan's signature and his address in Durham, North Carolina.

Almost three decades after entering Jordan's garage, the 550 Maranello changed hands again. This time, for $2.7 million. It wasn’t just a Ferrari that was sold: the car behind the Air Jordan XIV and one of the last great images of Michael Jordan as a Bulls player also went up for auction.

articles.title: “It don’t look good”: Karl-Anthony Towns admits contract talks with the Knicks stall despite his willingness to help
articles.standfirst: Like Brunson, Towns is willing to take a pay cut to help the Knicks maintain a competitive roster
articles.summary: Like Brunson, Towns is willing to take a pay cut to help the Knicks maintain a competitive roster
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are preparing to raise their championship banner and receive their hardware against the Philadelphia 76ers on opening night inside Madison Square Garden , but star center Karl-Anthony Towns admits that an extension is unlikely to materialize before the regular-season tip-off on October 20th .

Towns, who holds a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign , is technically eligible to lock in a massive four-year, $276 million extension .

However, league sources indicate that both sides remain significantly wide apart in negotiations, with current proposals from the front office falling into the $45 million to $50 million per year bracket rather than matching his maximum value demands.

Karl-Anthony Towns Admits Extension Talks Have Stalled

To preserve their championship core, sidestep the restrictive financial penalties of the second apron , and clear a path to hand Jalen Brunson his max extension next summer, New York requires financial flexibility that depends on players accepting team-friendly deals.

Towns stated that he remains open to taking less money to keep the roster together, provided that the organization properly values his contributions and the accomplishments achieved over the past two seasons.

“Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me,” Towns remarked. “None of those things have come close to happening.” When pressed by reporters on whether securing a deal should be straightforward given the team's historic success, his candid response was direct: “No s--t, Sherlock.”

Since arriving in Manhattan in 2024 , Towns has anchored a powerhouse squad that reached the conference finals before capturing the Knicks' first title in over 50 years.

He has maintained elite individual production, averaging 22.2 points and 12.3 rebounds per game , while shooting an impressive 39.5 percent from beyond the arc and is widely regarded as the NBA's premier stretch big man.

Many wondered if the team would finally move on from the enigmatic power forward, especially as his offensive contributions continue to dwindle.

With Green having a lot to prove this season, especially with a more important role on the team likely on the horizon, fans expected him to at least be in great shape ahead of the season . That isn't the case, though, at all.

Draymond Green looks out of shape by NBA standards with season nearing

Fans were critical of Green after an interview of his surfaced this week where he didn't look to be in the best shape , given that the season starts so soon.

The body shaming got out of control when some users used AI to create a video with Green having female breasts . Green is constantly on social media, so he's probably caught wind of the discourse already.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving goes all-in on his NBA comeback with new sneakers inspired by Macao’s high-stakes world
articles.standfirst: Two new signature sneakers arrive October 10, turning Kyrie’s anticipated return into a story of patience, calculated moves and refusing to fold
articles.summary: Two new signature sneakers arrive October 10, turning Kyrie’s anticipated return into a story of patience, calculated moves and refusing to fold
articles.body:
Kyrie Irving’s next move comes with hearts , spades and a message about trusting himself again. The Dallas Mavericks guard’s KAI 3 “Macao Hearts” and KAIBRID “Spades” launch October 10, 2026 , bringing a playing-card theme to his anticipated NBA comeback. Inspired by Macao’s bright lights and high-stakes atmosphere, the collection connects the instincts of a poker player with the creativity of one of basketball’s most unpredictable guards.

The release falls between Dallas’ preseason games against the Houston Rockets at The Venetian Arena on October 9 and 11 . Dallas Sports Journal reported that Irving’s footwear partner, ANTA, said he had been cleared to play without restrictions following his recovery from a torn left ACL. The shoes arrive as Irving prepares to return to NBA competition with the Dallas Mavericks.

Kyrie’s comeback gives “all-in” a meaning beyond the card table

The Spades concept compares Irving’s game to Texas Hold 'Em, a contest of patience, calculation and daring. It is an apt metaphor for a player who can slow a possession, draw a defender into committing and suddenly change direction. After a long recovery, that same patience becomes part of the story behind his return.

The KAIBRID blends design elements from the KAI 1, KAI 2 and KAI 3 , bringing three generations of his signature line into one hybrid silhouette. Its Spades edition combines blue and yellow with gold, bronze and black accents. Spade graphics appear on the tongue and insoles, while pearlized finishes, speckled textures and metallic details reference Macao’s skyline and nightlife.

The KAI 3 Hearts takes a different approach, with fluorescent red over a black base, metallic gold and color-shifting accents. The heart graphic reinforces the card theme, while the red represents Irving’s passion for basketball. These two releases begin a planned four-model Macao collection, with KAI 1 and KAI 2 editions expected in the coming months.

For U.S. shoppers, the buying options matter. KAI 3 Hearts will retail for 135throughANTA.com ,whilelimitedpairsofthe 150 KAIBRID Spades are scheduled exclusively for ANTA’s Beverly Hills flagship store. That exclusivity applies to the U.S. launch: the brand’s Malaysian website also lists Spades for October 10 pickup at its Kuala Lumpur store.

Behind the colors is a performance basketball platform. ANTA’s European product descriptions for other KAI 3 editions list NitroEdge foam cushioning, a carbon-fiber plate and a lightweight, breathable upper , designed to provide support during jumps and quick changes of direction.

Those features describe the broader KAI 3 model; complete specifications for the Macao editions have not been verified, and the KAIBRID’s hybrid design does not establish that it includes every technology from the earlier shoes.

Irving also has a role in shaping the company behind the collection. ANTA appointed him chief creative officer of its basketball division when their partnership was announced in July 2023. His responsibilities include developing products and bringing athletes, artists and other collaborators into the signature line. The relationship gives him influence over the creative direction of the brand he wears.

Fans will have two new pairs to choose from on October 10 . For Irving, the moment means returning to something he has worked toward throughout his recovery: stepping onto the court with his Dallas Mavericks teammates. Behind the bright colors and playing-card symbols of his new signature shoe are months of rehabilitation, determination and dedication, leading to the chance to wear his own design for his long-awaited return to the court.

articles.title: Stephen Curry honors Don Nelson, the coach who believed in him before the Warriors glory days
articles.standfirst: Curry’s “Nellie Night” message gave Golden State’s new jersey tribute a personal meaning
articles.summary: Curry’s “Nellie Night” message gave Golden State’s new jersey tribute a personal meaning
articles.body:
S tephen Curry took the microphone before the Warriors’ October 6 preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers to explain a new detail on Golden State’s jerseys . The name on the patch belonged to Don Nelson , the coach who guided his first NBA season. For Curry, honoring “Nellie” meant remembering where his own story with the franchise began.

“As you might notice, we have a new patch on our jersey this year to honor our former head coach Don Nelson,” Curry told the Chase Center crowd. The Warriors will wear the “Nellie” memorial band throughout the 2026–27 season in tribute to Nelson, who died August 9 at 86.

“He was my coach back in 2009,” Curry continued, acknowledging former players and members of Nelson’s family in attendance. “He was an icon in the NBA family but did so much for the Bay Area.”

Don Nelson’s last NBA season was Stephen Curry’s first

Their time together lasted just one season: 2009–10. Nelson was approaching the end of his coaching career, while Curry was beginning a journey whose destination neither could fully know. Years later, Curry credited Nelson with helping bring him to Golden State and giving him the opportunity to develop.

That belief extended to a decision that helped change the franchise. According to NBA reporting, Nelson and then-general manager Larry Riley jointly chose to keep Curry rather than trade his draft rights to Phoenix in a potential deal for Amar’e Stoudemire. The Warriors held on to the young guard who would eventually become the center of their championship years.

Curry gave them early reasons to believe . As a rookie under Nelson, he averaged 17.5 points, made 166 three-pointers and earned All-Rookie First Team honors, finishing second in Rookie of the Year voting. The achievements were smaller than those still to come, but they marked the beginning of something Golden State would grow to treasure.

Their shared season also gave Curry a memory he would carry for years. On April 7, 2010, Nelson secured his 1,333rd regular-season victory, passing Lenny Wilkens for the NBA coaching record. Curry was part of the team that celebrated the milestone in Minnesota. Nelson retired with 1,335 wins and remained the record holder until Gregg Popovich surpassed him in 2022.

Nelson’s connection to the Bay Area stretched across generations. He recorded 422 regular-season victories in 11 seasons with Golden State, overseeing the Run TMC era and returning to lead the 2007 “We Believe” Warriors. Their victory over the top-seeded Dallas Mavericks made them the first No. 8 seed to win a seven-game playoff series against a No. 1 seed.

His basketball ideas also endured. Nelson helped popularize the point-forward role and embraced unconventional lineups, finding possibilities in players beyond the positions traditionally assigned to them. His willingness to experiment helped shape a game increasingly built around versatility, spacing and creativity.

Golden State capped “Nellie Night” with a 124–98 preseason win over the Lakers. Curry finished with 16 points and five assists in just 14 minutes, shooting 4-of-7 from the field and making three of his six three-point attempts. The Warriors scored 45 points in the opening quarter and entered halftime ahead 81–53.

Yaxel Lendeborg led Golden State with 17 points and nine rebounds, while Brandin Podziemski added 16 points and Draymond Green delivered eight assists. Sandro Mamukelashvili paced the Lakers with 15 points. On a night devoted to remembering one of the franchise’s most influential coaches, the Warriors gave their home crowd a victory to celebrate, too.

Curry will wear Nelson’s name on his jersey all season. For him, it is a way to remember the coach who believed in him when he was just getting started and to keep him close each time he takes the court.

articles.title: LeBron's alleged scolding of Embiid for being late that outrages 'King' James: "It's a lie"'
articles.standfirst: Embiid hasn't arrived late, so stop the lies
articles.summary: Embiid hasn't arrived late, so stop the lies
articles.body:
leBron James has responded to the rumors that he had scolded Joel Embiid , his teammate on the Philadelphia 76ers, for arriving late to a 76ers practice .'

' "He wasn’t late, so stop the lies," the former Laker posted on his Instagram account.'

Embiid came onto the court a couple of minutes late and LeBron harshly scolded him

'LeBron James's reaction came after analyst Mike Breen reported, during the preseason game between the Sixers and Knicks, that LeBron harshly reprimanded Embiid in a recent practice after he arrived late to the session.'

"They were ready to practice, Joel Embiid came out onto the court a couple of minutes late, and LeBron harshly called him out," Breen recounted, saying that a source close to the Sixers' locker room told him.

'In 2024 Tyrese Maxey had already criticized Embiid for arriving late "to everything" and "challenged" him to be punctual .'

The only thing that matters is what we preach every day and how we're going to hold each other accountable

LeBron James and Joel Embiid face their first season with a Sixers team that aspires to everything with Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

"The only thing that matters is what we preach every day and how we're going to hold each other accountable," LeBron James made clear on his podcast "Mind the Game".

articles.title: Curry shows the Lakers that they are much less without Doncic: "It's not just about me"'
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Warriors comfortably defeat the Los Angeles Lakers, who played without Luka Doncic, in the NBA preseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors comfortably defeat the Los Angeles Lakers, who played without Luka Doncic, in the NBA preseason
articles.body:
Los Ángeles Lakers played without Luka Doncic 24 hours after beating the Sacramento Kings with the slovenian, and they paid for it'

The Golden State Warriors cruised past the Los Angeles team to claim a 124-98 win at the Chase Center in San Francisco in the NBA preseason.

Stephen Curry (16 points with 3 of 6 from three in 14 minutes) , Yaxel Lendeborg (17 points and 9 rebounds) and Brandin Podziemski (16 points) led the victory for the San Francisco Bay team.

The best for the Lakers were S andro Mamukelashvili (15 points) , Jaden Hardy (13 points), Quentin Grimes (12 points) and Dalton Knecht (11 points).

'Adou Thiero saves his knee after an out-of-this-world dunk and a bad fall: "It's hard to worry about the landing"'

Adou Thiero scored 7 points and 4 rebounds in his Lakers' loss.

The powerful 22-year-old forward, standing 2.01 m tall and having a 117-centimeter vertical leap , produced a spectacular dunk that frightened the crowd because of the shocking position his right leg was left in when he landed.

"It was a hard fall, but I'm fine. I will definitely pay more attention to that, although there are situations in which it's difficult to worry about the landing. But, of course, it's something I still keep in mind," he said after the game to reassure the fans.

'Regarding his jumping ability, Thiero shared that "I’ve been improving in that area over the course of the summer and learning to identify when to use my athleticism... There are also times when I can jump surrounded by three players and still get a dunk. It’s simply about having confidence in myself and knowing what I can do in each situation".'

'Luka Doncic: "Basketball is one of the best things in my life and I missed it a lot"'

The Lakers played without Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Collin Sexton.

'Doncic, who r eceived a blow to the thigh and did not play against the Warriors by technical decision, admitted after beating the Kings that "I felt very good. Basketball is one of the best things in my life and I missed it a lot. I think it has been five or six months. Playing and competing again is very fun for me, and I am really happy to have returned".'

"No"It's not just about me, but about how the team feels playing together. We've shown that we can play very well, especially in the transition from defense to offense, but I feel that we still have a lot of room for improvement. I'm very happy to be part of this team," he pointed out.'

articles.title: Khalifa Diop, everything for the NBA dream: "If I have to sleep in the arena... I'll do it"'
articles.standfirst: He looks for a spot in the NBA with the Cleveland Cavaliers
articles.summary: He looks for a spot in the NBA with the Cleveland Cavaliers
articles.body:
T he Cleveland Cavaliers have been in Spain to get ready for the new season. The NBA franchise has been working at the impressive "The Sanctuary" facilities on the Costa del Sol. Khalifa Diop, one of the new signings for the Ohio team, spoke to the microphones of "Nos Gusta el Basket".

The level of communication is incredible, they have people everywhere and that helps the player a lot, pointed out the Senegalese player, who previously played for Gran Canaria and Baskonia, clubs he still follows very closely. "The other day I was talking with Paolo Galbiatti, he's a guy who helped me a lot last year off the court as well . I'm also in contact with my teammates and following them."

The center, who is in the final stage of his journey, is about to share a locker room with players of the caliber of James Harden or Donovan Mitchell "They have a lot of experience and try to help you on every play or in the video room, and I’m going to learn a lot from them" , Khalifa said, fulfilling a dream with his signing for the CAVS. "It has always been my goal; every summer I would go with them to train, to work on individual skills, and this summer I tried everything possible to be with them and in the end I made it. Even if I have to sleep in the arena, I will do everything in my power to spend many years in the NBA" , he confessed.

He still has a tough preseason ahead of him to convince the "Madrilenian" Atkinson that there is room for him on the team. "The coach has asked me to help in every way I can, especially with rebounding and defending the pick-and-roll. This is a great team and I am here to help them achieve their goals," he explained.

'In Cleveland, the center also shares a team with a player he knows perfectly from many Liga Endesa matchups, Mario Hezonja , who is also fighting for a spot among the chosen ones. "What can I tell you about Mario? He is one of the best players in Europe, MVP of the Liga Endesa, and is more than ready for the NBA" , he said.'

articles.title: Aday Mara lands on his feet with the Thunder: "You have to be in very good shape to do those things"
articles.standfirst: The Spanish center makes his preseason debut, is praised by his coach, and gets his teammates off the bench with his plays
articles.summary: The Spanish center makes his preseason debut, is praised by his coach, and gets his teammates off the bench with his plays
articles.body:
"E The first preseason game for Aday Mara with the Thunder could not have left a better impression on his teammates , on his coach Mark Daigneault , on the Oklahoma press, and on the fans. Starting and in just 18 minutes on the court, the Spanish center scored 12 points without a miss (5/5 from the field), 12 points, nine rebounds, three assists, and three blocks . In that time he showed the breadth of his repertoire. Oklahoma, without many of their key players, ended up losing 110-116.

Thunder coach especially highlighted the effort Mara has made over the summer to get into shape. "He worked very hard from the end of Summer League until he returned to Oklahoma and then through training camp. There were many days he spent with his head down, working on his physical conditioning, and it showed tonight," Daigneault said about his pupil, selected with the 12th pick in the latest draft.

Both on offense and defense, Mara was able to show his main assets: great court vision and passing ability, easy baskets by making the most of his height and technical fundamentals, and rim protection. "Obviously he is a very effective player because of his skill level on offense and then because of his impact on defense, but you have to be in very good shape to do those things and he is working on that" , said the Thunder coach, who summed it up in one sentence: "It was a very good start for him" .

At the start of the second quarter, the Zaragoza-born center produced one of the plays that define his game. He blocked a shot under his own basket, took off on the break, received a pass in stride, and headed to the rim to finish with a beautiful extended layup . At 2.21 meters tall, there are not many players in the NBA capable of doing that.

The Thunder bench, amazed

Chet Holmgren, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams, and the rest of the bench got up to celebrate it . Some with a look of disbelief and others imitating Mara's brilliant finish. "I saw it, I saw it. It was funny . They were doing the "finger roll" gesture. I was just there, I got the ball, saw the rim, and I didn't even think I could dunk it, so I tried to make a layup. It was fun" , said the Spanish player.

It was his first preseason game and it's not wise to overreact, since the regular season is a different story, but starting out by showing everyone what you're capable of is extraordinary news .

articles.title: Stephen Curry confided in Steve Kerr months ago about real reason he'll never leave the Warriors
articles.standfirst: Golden State’s franchise star made clear that his connection to the team goes far beyond basketball
articles.summary: Golden State’s franchise star made clear that his connection to the team goes far beyond basketball
articles.body:
The question of whether Stephen Curry could ever finish his career somewhere other than the Golden State Warriors has lingered around the NBA whenever the franchise has faced uncertainty.

According to Steve Kerr , Curry settled that question privately months ago.

“When we talked at the end of last year, I asked him if that was a consideration,” Kerr said. “First thing he said was, I’m not moving my family. My family is so important to me, and they’re happy here. And he said, I don’t want to go anywhere.”

Curry’s wife, Ayesha Curry , and their four children — Riley, Ryan, Canon and Caius — have built their lives in the Bay Area while he has spent his entire professional career with Golden State .

“And that’s a reflection of who he is as a father, as a human being,” Kerr added. “And he meant that for his own personal family and his Warriors family, too.”

Curry’s loyalty never in question

Curry has since reinforced that commitment by agreeing to a two-year extension reportedly worth $116 million, keeping him under contract through the 2028-29 season.

Kerr said the possibility of Curry leaving never felt particularly realistic to those around him.

“Honestly, the beauty of Steph is that there’s never been a moment where any of us thought he was leaving,” Kerr said. “I mean, he’s that locked in with his teammates, his coaches, management, his family. I can feel it. He doesn’t want to go anywhere else.”

The coach believes Curry also understands the significance of spending an entire career with one franchise.

“He’s going to be Kobe for the Lakers, Tim Duncan for the Spurs,” Kerr said. “Steph will always be the Warriors, and that’s pretty cool.”

Curry was drafted by Golden State in 2009 and has since won four championships and two MVP awards while becoming the defining player of the franchise’s most successful era.

Relationship with Kerr goes beyond winning

Kerr is entering his 13th season coaching Curry , and his admiration for the guard extends well beyond what he has accomplished on the court.

“I can’t even imagine a coach being luckier ever in the history of the game than I am to coach Steph Curry,” Kerr said. “Not just the player, but the human being. He brings light to every room that he’s in, even in the dark times.”

Curry has expressed a similar attachment to the Bay Area, describing it as home and making clear that finishing his career with the Warriors remains important to him.

That helps explain why Kerr ’s question about leaving produced such an immediate response. Curry ’s decision wasn't simply about staying with the organization that drafted him.

It was about protecting the life his family has built there, and keeping together both the family at home and the basketball family that has surrounded him for nearly two decades.

articles.title: Bronny James and Stephen Curry's reaction after a controversial refereeing decision
articles.standfirst: The reaction of both during the Lakers vs. Warriors drew attention after a refereeing decision that involved the young Los Angeles player.
articles.summary: The reaction of both during the Lakers vs. Warriors drew attention after a refereeing decision that involved the young Los Angeles player.
articles.body:
B ronny James and Stephen Curry starred in one of the most curious moments of the matchup between the Los Angeles Lakers and Golden State Warriors . In the middle of the game, a refereeing decision sparked a reaction between the two that quickly drew attention.

The incident occurred when Bronny was called for an offensive foul while Curry was defending him . The situation ended with the two players laughing, in a scene that some interpreted as an ironic reaction to one of the new rules the NBA is applying.

The play that made Bronny and Curry laugh

The play happened when Bronny tried to use his arm to create separation while driving. The referees ruled that he had committed a violation and called an offensive foul.

The NBA is paying special attention this season to so-called “push-offs,” when a player uses the free arm to push or create separation from their defender.

The decision generated an immediate reaction from the Lakers player. Curry, who was directly involved in the play as the defender, also ended up laughing along with Bronny, giving rise to one of the most eye-catching moments of the night.

The scene did not go unnoticed because it came in a game that pitted two of the most popular NBA franchises against each other. In addition, the interpretation of the play once again put the spotlight on the new provisions that seek to limit certain moves by attacking players.

What changes with the NBA’s “new rule”

Although people are talking about a new rule, the NBA has not created a foul that was previously allowed. The league included pushes with the off arm among its points of emphasis for the 2026-27 season: this is about reinforcing the enforcement of a prohibition that was already in the rulebook.

The focus is on the so-called push-offs , moves in which the attacker uses the arm not controlling the ball to push the defender and gain space. Moving the opponent out of position to make a shot or a drive easier constitutes an offensive foul , not a legal way to get open. Contact to feel the opponent’s position is still allowed; forcefully pushing him or fully extending the arm against him is not.

When this offensive foul is called, the player is charged with a personal foul and their team loses possession. The opponent inbound from the sideline, with no free throws for that infraction. The penalty, therefore, not only interrupts the shot attempt: it also ends the opportunity to attack .

Bronny is not the only one who has encountered this criterion during preparation. Scottie Barnes was also penalized for a similar action in Toronto's preseason opener. According to Sporting News, the Raptors player described the distinction between allowed and penalized contact as “strange” .

articles.title: Damage control? Mike Breen backtracks on controversial comments about Lebron James following Embiid's reaction
articles.standfirst: What was supposed to highlight leadership turned into one of Philadelphia’s first preseason distractions
articles.summary: What was supposed to highlight leadership turned into one of Philadelphia’s first preseason distractions
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are still in preseason, but one off-court story has already generated more attention than anything that happened in their opening game.

During the fourth quarter of Philadelphia’s 120-97 win over the New York Knicks , Mike Breen said he had been told that Joel Embiid arrived a couple of minutes late to practice and that LeBron James immediately called him out.

“Somebody told me before the game that they were out ready to practice, and Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple of minutes late, and LeBron let him hear it,” Breen said on the broadcast.

The story spread quickly because of Embiid’s previous history with questions about punctuality and accountability. James, however, rejected it outright.

“He ain’t been late so stop the lies,” James wrote on Instagram.

Point was never to criticize Embiid

Breen addressed the fallout Wednesday and said his intention had been almost the opposite of how the story was received.

“I’m so disappointed how the story was interpreted,” Breen told ESPN. “The whole intent was praising LeBron for already having an impact on the team’s professionalism and accountability, even something so benign as a player getting on the court for practice a minute or two late.”

Breen said the anecdote came from “someone I trust” and that he believed it illustrated how quickly James was establishing himself as a leader in Philadelphia.

“I thought it would be an interesting anecdote to show LeBron’s leadership already on display in Philly,” Breen said.

He also admitted that using Embiid ’s name gave the story a weight he hadn't anticipated.

“In hindsight, I should have realized the fact that it was Joel is what made it a story,” Breen said. “I’ve always been a huge fan of Joel and feel awful that it put the focus on him the way that it did.”

Nurse backs Embiid as Sixers try to move on

Breen ultimately accepted James ’ denial and walked back his original comments about Embiid .

“I don’t know why the person who told me the story would make it up, but if LeBron says it never happened then I believe him and apologize for putting it out there,” Breen admitted.

Head coach Nick Nurse also pushed back on any suggestion that Embiid had been a problem during camp.

“I’m just surprised by what I was told before and what you guys are asking me about, because he’s been excellent,” Nurse said. “He’s in great shape; he’s been on the practice floor. He’s worked very hard and he looks really great.”

The Sixers would clearly prefer the focus to return to basketball. James, Embiid and Tyrese Maxey all sat out the Knicks game, with Nurse planning to use more of his intended regular-season rotation in the remaining preseason schedule.

What began as a complimentary story about James ’ leadership instead became a lesson in how quickly one anecdote can take on a life of its own.

articles.title: NBA and FIBA's response to the EuroLeague's no: NBA Europe moves forward
articles.standfirst: Both bodies issue a statement following the decision of the EuroLeague General Assembly
articles.summary: Both bodies issue a statement following the decision of the EuroLeague General Assembly
articles.body:
The NBA and FIBA broke their silence after the Euroleague General Assembly at Lake Como and the rejection by the 13 owner teams of an offer to achieve a united front.

NBA and FIBA issued a statement this Thursday in response to that decision in which, above all, it is clear that both entities will move forward with the NBA Europe project with or without the EuroLeague . Although the idea of the 13 teams is to continue negotiating , NBA and FIBA state in their statement that " they remain committed to moving forward with a new men's professional league in Europe ".

'Although the statement is clear, it also mentions that the ideal scenario would be an agreement among the three parties to " unify the European basketball ecosystem ".'

At Lake Como, the teams rejected the NBA's offer , but even though some teams wanted to stop negotiating, the majority leaned toward continuing to listen to the other side and keeping the path of negotiation open. This is the full statement from the NBA and FIBA:

"A partnership among the EuroLeague, FIBA, and the NBA to unify the European basketball ecosystem would unlock the enormous potential of the game across Europe for the benefit of clubs, players, and, most importantly, fans. The NBA and FIBA remain committed to moving forward with a new professional men's league in Europe and helping to build a stronger and more sustainable basketball ecosystem together with partners who share our vision of growth, opportunity, and the fundamental principles of the European sports model".
